title: Remark
body_md: The square reference grid provides a convenient baseline for more general formation geometries. For a nonsquare or irregular arrangement, the Fraunhofer distance can be estimated using an enclosing square aperture. Within the same transverse-aperture criterion, this gives a conservative estimate and avoids deriving a separate expression for every configuration. Configuration-specific expressions can nevertheless provide tighter estimates by accounting for the actual occupied positions, as in the case of the cross-shaped configuration considered in \cite{RdG_2025}.
head: environment
name: Fraunhofer Distance for General Formations

title: Remark
body_md: In distributed satellite systems, the low \acl{SNR} of individual radiating elements can make direct estimation of all channel coefficients impractical. Precoding therefore often relies on channel reconstruction from user-location and satellite-state information, using an assumed propagation model. The distinction between the reconstructed channel $\widetilde{\mathbf{h}}_k$ and the propagation channel $\mathbf{h}_k$ thus reflects a practical design issue. If reconstruction uses a global \ac{FF} approximation while users lie in the formation's radiative \ac{NF}, a modeling mismatch remains even with perfect geometric information. Our comparison isolates the performance penalty caused by this operationally relevant mismatch from that due to parameter-estimation errors.
head: environment
name: Practical relevance of precoding mismatch
